new_statements.translation: 2.2.4. Note that, for the other languages of this set, Nkwele, Doe, Zalamo, Kutu, Kami (group XVII) and most Swahili dialects (group XVIII) have completely lost all prosodic distinctiveness and have only a demarcative accent on the penultimate. [p. 483:] a) languages with culmination of length and pitch on the penultimate (languages with no distinctive prosodemes and no length opposition): ... nkwele, doe, zalamo, kutu, kami; several Swahili dialects.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Doe (Kidoe), like Kami, Kutu, Zaramo, Kwere and Swahili, has no lexical tone and uses stress instead; the visible snippet does not say where the stress falls (the comparison class is 'simple stress (e.g. Kiswahili)', i.e. penultimate, but that is not stated for Kidoe in the text seen).
new_statements.identity_note: 'Kidoe' listed together with Kikami, Kikutu, Kizaramo and Kikwere, i.e. the East Ruvu neighbours of the Tanzanian coast hinterland = Doe doee1238 (not Ekoid Ndoe). The book is about Swahili origins; the Doe remark is a secondhand areal generalisation by a UDSM Kiswahili scholar, not first-hand Doe fieldwork.
